hero.name: Merijn Kersten
hero.subheading: Building things that survive outside the demo room

capabilitiesIntro.title: From the scale of a city to that of a chip
capabilitiesIntro.lead: I tend to bounce between three sizes of thing.

workIntro.lead: A pile of projects from over the years. Some ended up on thousands of phones, some were beautiful failures. All of them taught me something, so I’ve kept the lesson stapled to it.

about.title: From shaders to screws
about.lead: I’m a creative technologist from Utrecht. I've been working on it for about a decade, and I still get the same kick out of it: take some upcoming technology and push it until it does something slightly magical.
body: I’m happiest somewhere between the screen and the physical world. I’ll jump from a shader to a backend to a soldering iron on the same day. I like seeing the whole thing, context is everything. A lot of what I make is really about connecting the digital and the physical so they stop feeling like separate worlds.

Most of what I actually know came from side projects and things that broke in interesting ways. I like grabbing tech before it’s really ready — ARKit and ARCore back when you still had to glue them together yourself, multiplayer AR, visual positioning, Vision Pro, whatever the new shiny thing is.

I have some opinions, and here’s the big one: the demo always lies. Something that works flawlessly on my desk will find a hundred new ways to break when it meets a real network, hardware, or person who didn’t read the manual.
Right now I’m connecting VR players without crossing wires (a real challenge it turns out) and a couple of side projects. If any of that sounds fun, come say hi!

contact.title: Let’s build something cool together
contact.lead: I’m always up for a chat, drop me a line.
